intro: After a category is observed, its probability in a Bayesian predictive sequence changes. Track those changing probabilities instead of multiplying one fixed distribution.
task: Score an ordered category sequence under a Dirichlet prior, updating the concentration vector after each observation.
requirements: alpha is a vector of concentrations in [1e-8,1e6]. observations is a nonempty vector of integer-valued category IDs in [0,len(alpha)-1].
Before each update, probability=concentration[category]/sum(concentration). Record it, add its logarithm to the sequence log probability, then increment that category concentration by one.
Return {"probabilities": per-step vector, "log_probability": scalar, "posterior": final concentration vector}. Score the supplied ordered sequence; do not multiply by a multinomial counting factor.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Read the probability of the next observed category before incrementing its concentration.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Accumulate logarithms along the ordered sequence; a multinomial coefficient would count additional sequences that were not supplied.

explanation: Each observation changes the next predictive distribution because the concentration vector accumulates evidence. A repeated category becomes more probable than it was under the initial prior.

Although individual step probabilities depend on order, the product for a complete ordered sequence depends only on its category counts. A count-event probability would also include how many different sequences have those counts.
